description: We are final-year B.Tech engineering students passionate about Space Exploration and applied software engineering. Combining skills in Web Development, AI & Machine Learning, Data Analysis, Data Visualization, and Design, we are tackling the "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions" challenge. Our platform pairs predictive anomaly detection with intuitive telemetry dashboards to help deep-space crews track vitals, detect early health risks, and stay mission-ready.
summary: ASTRA-MED is a full-stack, zero-hardware-required autonomous AI Flight Surgeon application engineered for long-duration deep-space missions. During transits to Mars or the Lunar Gateway, communication delays with Earth reach up to 44 minutes, preventing real-time ground medical intervention during acute physiological emergencies.   To bridge this gap, ASTRA-MED continuously monitors 13 cross-correlated bio-telemetric vitals alongside daily astronaut self-check-ins across NASA’s four core spaceflight risk domains: cardiovascular events, immune and radiation exposure, musculoskeletal deconditioning, and behavioral health. Powered by a dual-model machine learning engine—combining an Isolation Forest anomaly detector with a 7-day multi-domain risk forecaster—the system pairs Explainable AI (XAI) vital-deviation alerts with actionable NASA clinical countermeasure protocols. Featuring an interactive anatomical telemetry HUD and gamified XP adherence tracking, ASTRA-MED empowers crews to autonomously safeguard health and mission readiness in deep space.
details:
Overview & What It Does

ASTRA-MED is a zero-hardware-required, full-stack autonomous AI Flight Surgeon system engineered to protect astronaut health during long-duration deep-space missions (such as Earth-to-Mars transits and Lunar Gateway operations). When round-trip communication delays with Earth reach 22 to 44 minutes, crews cannot rely on real-time ground flight surgeons during acute medical events. ASTRA-MED bridges this gap by continuously monitoring 13 cross-correlated bio-telemetric channels alongside daily astronaut self-check-ins across NASA’s four core spaceflight risk domains:

  • Cardiovascular Events: Cephalad fluid shifts, orthostatic intolerance, resting tachycardia, and baroreceptor desensitization.
  • Immune & Radiation Exposure: Galactic Cosmic Ray (GCR) and Solar Particle Event (SPE) dosage tracking (mSv), core temperature spikes ("space fever"), and inflammatory reactions.
  • Bone & Musculoskeletal Deconditioning: Microgravity bone mineral density (BMD) decay, sarcomere atrophy, and Advanced Resistive Exercise Device (ARED) compliance.
  • Behavioral Health: Circadian desynchrony, sleep architecture disruption, cognitive reaction latency, and isolation stress.

How It Works (Dual-Engine ML & Explainable AI)

  • Unsupervised Multi-Vital Anomaly Detection (IsolationForest): Screens 13 physiological parameters against calibrated microgravity baselines, outputting a real-time anomaly score (0.00 nominal to 1.00 critical) to catch subtle multi-variable departures early.
  • Multi-Domain Risk Forecaster (RandomForestRegressor / GradientBoosting): Predicts 7-day forward risk trajectories (0–100%) across all four health pillars and computes a composite Astronaut Mission Health Readiness score.
  • Explainable AI (XAI) Attribution: Identifies the exact physiological drivers behind alerts using Z-scores and baseline percentage deltas (e.g., "+14% resting HR & -2.1h sleep debt").
  • Autonomous Countermeasure Recommender: Pairs elevated risk states with actionable NASA clinical protocols—such as 500mL isotonic fluid loading with Class II compression garments, storm shelter relocation, eccentric ARED squats, or 480nm circadian spectrum lighting resets.

Key Benefits & Intended Impact ASTRA-MED shifts spaceflight medicine from reactive, Earth-dependent tele-monitoring to proactive, autonomous onboard care. Because it operates purely on existing spacecraft telemetry and crew self-reports without requiring new medical hardware, it is immediately deployable on resource-constrained vehicles—safeguarding crew survival, cognitive performance, and mission success on 180+ day journeys.

Tools, Technologies & Architecture

  • Backend & AI/ML: Python, FastAPI (REST API & Server-Sent Events live streaming), Scikit-Learn (IsolationForest, RandomForestRegressor, GradientBoosting), NumPy/Pandas, and a custom 180-day NASA physiological telemetry simulator with 4 clinical scenario presets.
  • Frontend Mission Console: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts (7-day predictive trajectory charts), and custom interactive SVG visualizations.
  • Hardware: Zero specialized external hardware required; runs on standard onboard flight laptops or tablets.

Creativity & Human-Centered Design Factors Beyond clinical accuracy, our team considered 180+ day psychological disengagement and cognitive load during emergencies:

  • Interactive SVG Anatomical Telemetry Map: Provides an instant visual scan of pulsing risk zones on the human body with one-click organ/system drilldowns.
  • Clinical Trust via XAI: Rather than acting as a "black box," every alert explains why a risk is rising in plain clinical terms so astronauts can trust the recommendation under pressure.
  • Gamified Crew Adherence: Incorporates a Mission Health Streak and Readiness XP reward system (+50 XP for daily check-ins; +100 to +200 XP for completing countermeasures) to sustain long-term compliance and morale in isolated environments.
